title: CRM contact sync locking customer records

verification.methodology: pact business verification (database + checkout SLO + protected ops)

checks.name: database_clear
checks.detail: No lock waits: no session is blocked.

audit.report: The batch_replayable_crm_contact_sync job (pid 1298632) went idle in transaction for 4.2 seconds while holding locks, blocking 12 sessions and collapsing checkout to 0% success (121/121 failed) with $18,400/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the job — classified as BATCH_REPLAYABLE with a 10-minute replay cost and may_interrupt policy — because waiting for its ~596s remaining runtime would cost ~$182,712 and exceed the 60-second degradation tolerance. The Continuity Guardian accepted without objection, and the pact was sealed in one round. Termination executed successfully; verification confirmed checkout recovered to 100% success (36/36 over 10s), no lock waits remain, and protected operations were intact.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_crm_contact_sync job (pid 1298632) entered an idle-in-transaction state while holding locks, blocking 12 sessions and causing checkout to collapse to 0% success.
lessons: For batch_replayable_crm_contact_sync: Add an idle-in-transaction timeout or guard to prevent jobs from holding locks indefinitely when stalled (the job was idle 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1).

For batch_replayable_crm_contact_sync: Pre-register it as an interruptible workload in the registry so future negotiations can skip the workload registry probe round, given its BATCH_REPLAYABLE class, 10-min replay cost, and may_interrupt policy.

For batch_replayable_crm_contact_sync: Add monitoring for idle-in-transaction states on batch replayable jobs as a leading indicator — this job showed SELECT 1 as its last statement while holding locks for 4.2s before detection.
audit.negotiation_critique: The negotiation was efficient — completed in one round with both guardians aligning on the trade-off (waiting costs $182,712 vs 10-minute replay). The Database Guardian provided complete evidence (lock state, checkout collapse, trade-off math) and the Continuity Guardian accepted without objection, correctly recognizing the BATCH_REPLAYABLE classification and may_interrupt policy.
follow_ups: Add an idle-in-transaction timeout to the batch_replayable_crm_contact_sync job configuration to prevent recurrence.
Review all BATCH_REPLAYABLE workloads for similar idle-in-transaction vulnerability and register them as pre-approved interruptible.
Add alerting for sessions idle in transaction > 5s holding locks on checkout-critical tables.
